subject: POC success criteria & evaluation roadmap — PacePoint Health
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@pacepointhealth.com>; Tom Li <tom.li@pacepointhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: proposed POC objectives & success metrics

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Per our call, I wanted to put a concise plan on paper so we have alignment before we kick off the POC next week. Below is a recommended success criteria and evaluation roadmap. Please flag anything you want changed.

Summary of intent:
- POC scope: Integrate Redwood hosted inference into PacePoint's triage assistant for clinical intake (replace current heuristic pipeline for initial symptom parsing).
- Timeline: 3-week technical POC (engineering integration + closed test set evaluation), followed by 2-week pilot in staging with synthetic and redacted real queries.

Proposed Success Criteria (must-haves to pass POC):
1) Latency: p95 inference latency (end-to-end, request received -> response returned) <= 250 ms for single-turn API calls under expected UI load.
2) Throughput: Sustained throughput of 200 requests/sec with <5% tail latency degradation when simulated workload matches expected spike patterns.
3) Cost: Effective cost per token <= $0.0035 (target) during evaluation; monthly extrapolated cost estimate provided at close of POC.
4) Quality: Automated eval on golden set: top-1 intent accuracy >= 82% and entity extraction F1 >= 0.78. Hallucination/incorrect-personalization rate <= 2%.
5) Security/Privacy: All inference traffic must remain in us-west region and log retention complies with your data retention policy (we'll use VPC options if needed).

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Week 0 (kickoff): runbook, access, and data handoff.
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests; baseline measurements for latency and cost with small test set.
- Week 2: run evaluation harness (golden set of ~1,200 queries, diversity across intent/length); collect latency distribution, token usage, and qualitative failure cases.
- Week 3: optimize model settings (batching/quantization suggestions), re-run evals, hand off results and recommended configuration.

Ownership / Next steps:
- Redwood: integration support (Mateo), evaluation harness and baseline reports (Laura).
- PacePoint: provide redacted sample queries (Samantha) and acceptance criteria sign-off (Tom).

Attachments (initial): POC-Statement-of-Work.pdf (sow outline), POC-MAP.pdf (milestone plan), Eval-Checklist.xlsx (metric definitions).

Requested: Can you confirm by EOD Monday that the latency/quality targets are reasonable and that you can provide a redacted sample set of ~1k queries by the Week 0 kickoff? Once we have that, I'll send a formal SOW and calendar invites.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@pacepointhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@pacepointhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: proposed POC objectives & success metrics

Thanks Dylan — this is very helpful and aligned. A couple quick notes from our side after syncing with the product team:

- Latency: for our clinician-facing UI we prefer p95 <= 150 ms if achievable; we understand that may require configuration tweaks (smaller batch windows / lower max-seq). If 150 ms is infeasible for the first run, p95 <= 250 ms is acceptable as a secondary milestone.
- Cost: target cost/token of $0.0025 instead of $0.0035 if we can get within that band after quantization suggestions.
- Quality: the thresholds look good; we will add a small manual annotation pass for edge-case logs during Week 2.
- Data residency: must be us-west region and we'd like to review the proposed log retention (30 days preferred for POC).

We can provide a redacted set of ~1,200 queries by Tue EOD if that works. We're available to kickoff Wed 23 Jul 2025 at 10:00 PT.

Samantha Ross
Director, Product — Clinical Systems
PacePoint Health

Subject: Re: Post-demo: proposed POC objectives & success metrics

Looping in engineering. Mateo and I went through Dylan's plan and Samantha's note — looks good. Quick implementation notes and owners: 

- Mateo (SE) will own the integration/runbook, create the evaluation harness, and instrument latency/throughput telemetry. Mateo will also provide the first pass on batching/quantization profiles.
- I'll produce a short evaluation playbook that maps the automated metrics to acceptance checks and manual review steps.
- Attachments I uploaded: POC-MAP.pdf (detailed milestones), Eval-Checklist.xlsx (metric definitions & golden set schema). I also attached a sample SLOs.xlsx with suggested alert thresholds.

Evaluation specifics Mateo will deliver during Week 2:
- Measurement suite: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency histograms (end-to-end), throughput traces under synthetic spike loads, and token accounting per-request.
- Quality checks: automated scoring against golden set (accuracy, F1), confusion-matrix artifacts, and a small manual review spreadsheet for hallucinations.
- Dataset size: target 1,200 labeled queries (we'll use 1,000 for automated metrics, 200 for manual review).

We will also provide a one-page runbook for how to toggle between model variants and how to enable VPC logging for you to validate retention.

Mateo, can you confirm the test harness template you'll use and if you need any special credentials from PacePoint ahead of Wed?

Thanks — Laura
